findings.description: The evidence_class vocabulary is not pinned as one closed set: F002 names terminal_transcript and contract_test, while F003 emits cli_transcript and contract_check, so captured agent evidence can fail the checker and close gate.

F004 adds required_data_sources to journeys but does not specify where evidence records structured data_source, availability, provenance, and capability_unavailable assertions, making keyed cross-surface comparison underspecified.
F001 allows consumer=both, but F005 only describes enforcement for journeys declaring consumer in {human, agent}, leaving the required per-family close-time proof for both ambiguous.
The required_evidence_classes API collapses surface, consumer, and claim kind even though mutation and qualitative claims are not surface classes and may share a surface with read-only claims.

The contract says real-or-honestly-degraded data can prove readiness and F004 says honest degradation passes, but F005 requires at least one real non-seeded end-to-end journey, so degraded close behavior is unresolved.
F005 relies on explicit non-goal deferral and operator disposition to allow close, but the plan does not define the structured fields or validation needed to distinguish them from ordinary prose.
F003 says typed-skip may use data_provenance=degraded or a skip marker, but F001 only permits seeded, real, or degraded, so the skip representation could violate the schema.

The surface taxonomy is still not deterministic enough for lock: F001 says to map the existing 8 qa-sufficiency surface classes, while F002 moves mutation out of surfaces into claim_kind and introduces names like cli_human, mcp_tool, and api without pinning the canonical surface_class enum.

The required-evidence rule uses ambiguous set notation for alternatives, such as screenshot|recording|journey_walk and tool_call_transcript|contract_check, structured_error, so implementers can disagree on whether all classes, any class, or a fallback-specific class is required.

F005 names completion_auditor enforcement but does not pin the actual close-path integration points in the existing platform, where auditing and plan close are separate concerns; a finding file alone would not guarantee that product-class close is blocked.

The advisory posture for substrate plans is under-specified against the current schemas: objective contracts currently accept only product goal types, substrate plans need not declare contracts, and F005 has an opted_in parameter without a declared schema or frontmatter source.

Typed-skip evidence and honest in-journey capability-unavailable evidence can share the same structured tuple of availability=unavailable and data_provenance=degraded, yet F004 and F005 require different close outcomes depending on whether a real journey execution also occurred.

F005 has a contradictory enforcement cell for substrate plans that declare consumer journeys. One test says the unflagged substrate plan only warns, while the activation and no-dodge rules say any consumer-journey-bearing plan blocks when unproven.

The F002 requirement expression for agent_mcp_tool read_only appears to require structured_error in addition to a tool transcript or contract check. That conflicts with the journey promise that a successful tool-call or contract transcript satisfies the claim.

The plan maps each surface_class to one family, but it does not pin validation between declared consumer and declared surfaces. A consumer=both journey could be declared with only a human surface, or an agent journey with only read_only_ui, leaving required evidence derivation ambiguous.

Product-class activation is pinned, but the plan does not state what happens when a product-class objective has no declared consumer journey. That leaves a dodge path where the gate activates but has no consumer outcome to evaluate.

F001 leaves data_source optional even when availability is present, but F004 depends on keyed availability/provenance comparison. An unavailable EvidenceRef without data_source cannot prove honest degradation or participate in cross-surface agreement.

The F003 acceptance requires typed-skip evidence to carry an operator-readable reason, but the schema changes and tests do not pin where that reason lives or that it is asserted. This risks silent unavailable skips that are structurally valid but operationally opaque.

F001's D034 pending rule allows consumer=both plans with agent proven but human not_yet_typed to close unblocked, while the objective contract says consumer=both requires both families proven and a missing family raises consumer_outcome_unproven unless structurally deferred or dispositioned.

The proposed deterministic gate signature lists contract, evidence, goal_type, opted_in, and dispositions, but omits product_metadata even though product metadata is one of the required activation paths and posture inputs.

The feature text defines structured non-goal deferral, but the enumerated tests only cover structured operator disposition; they do not prove that structured deferral allows close or that prose-only deferral is rejected.
The required advisory cell for a substrate plan activated solely by experience_readiness_opt_in with no declared consumer journeys is described but not pinned in the test list.

F001 registers consumer_outcome_unproven in the gap taxonomy, but does not equivalently specify taxonomy, severity, and output shape for no_consumer_journey_declared even though the contract requires that finding.

The sentence saying internal substrate plans are advisory unless opted in conflicts with the later D030 rule that any consumer-journey-bearing substrate plan blocks and only opt-in-with-no-journeys warns.

F001's D034/D035 pending rule lets consumer=both close when the agent family is proven but the human family is not_yet_typed, while the objective contract says consumer=both requires both families proven and a missing family yields consumer_outcome_unproven unless structurally deferred or dispositioned.

Product metadata is listed as an activation and posture input, but the proposed feature does not define the concrete metadata keys, parser, or close_plan wiring that makes product/migration/readiness/ux/consumer-facing delivery deterministic.

The required evidence calls for product-class blocking on substrate-only evidence, but the listed tests cover API-only, seeded-only, typed-skip-only, real capture, and degraded honesty without a dedicated substrate-only product-class close-block case.

F001 still contains stale substrate-posture wording saying the same unproven consumer gap on a substrate plan warns, while the contract and later D030 text require any consumer-journey-bearing plan, including substrate, to block unless structurally deferred or dispositioned.

The delivery_class parser is specified only for valid enum values and absent metadata. An invalid frontmatter value is not pinned, so a typo could be treated like absent/substrate and weaken the product_metadata activation path.
The contract requires posture-matrix evidence, but F001 lists scenario tests rather than a complete matrix over opt_in, has_consumer_journey, product-class goal_type, and product_metadata.

The real execution requirement is per objective claim per declared consumer, but the proposed tests do not pin objective-keyed grouping or prevent one real execution from satisfying multiple journeys that share a data_source.
F001 records consumer_outcome_pending as structured advisory state, but it does not pin the taxonomy/output shape the way it does for consumer_outcome_unproven and no_consumer_journey_declared.
